relations.rationale: Jun being head judge is consistent with and gives reason for Jun setting the pace others followed.
Jun's role as head judge has no bearing on whether the group settled into tents by evening.
Dara arriving later than Esme is consistent with Dara being out of breath from jogging to catch up, though not directly implied.
Dara's late arrival relative to Esme has no connection to clouds prompting a faster pace later.
Dara's breathlessness from jogging is unrelated to Jun's arrival before departure.
Dara's jogging and breathlessness earlier has no bearing on the group settling into tents by evening.
Eli's greater height directly supports the claim that his height made him useful for spotting distant markers.
Eli's height is unrelated to the group reaching a rocky outcrop for lunch.
Eli's height relative to the group has no bearing on who is youngest.
Eli's usefulness for spotting markers is unrelated to the group being ready to rest.
Yara bringing the first-aid kit is unrelated to whether Esme and Dara were on different teams.
Yara bringing the first-aid kit is unrelated to the group pausing at a stream to refill water.
Both suggest Yara's responsible, prepared nature, so carrying the kit supports her also tracking time carefully.
Yara bringing a first-aid kit has no bearing on clouds gathering over distant peaks.
Jun arriving last is consistent with and explained by Jun taking a wrong turn, supporting that account.
Jun arriving last among the group is consistent with still arriving before the group set off, since these describe compatible timing.
Jun arriving last is unrelated to whether Jun set the hiking pace.
Taking a wrong turn could have delayed Jun but is compatible with still arriving before departure, so it doesn't contradict but somewhat supports the timing account.
Jun's wrong turn near the visitor center is unrelated to the later stop at the rocky outcrop for lunch.
Jun's wrong turn has no bearing on who is youngest.
